items: Score Your Client History: Pull your last 8-10 client relationships and gather their project files, invoices, and correspondence to begin your analysis.

Score Your Client History: Score each client across 5 profitability factors including effective hourly rate, communication overhead, scope creep history, payment reliability, and whether you'd work with them again.
Score Your Client History: Identify your top 3 most profitable clients by looking for those who had high effective rates, low revision cycles, no scope creep, and paid on time.
Score Your Client History: Document the 2-3 shared characteristics of your best clients such as industry, company size, budget range, how they found you, or their decision-making process.
Build Your Avatar Document: Write out answers to 7 specific questions about your ideal client including their industry, company size, decision-making process, budget range, and how they find vendors.
Build Your Avatar Document: Describe the specific problem your ideal client is trying to solve right now and what a bad vendor experience has looked like for them in the past.
Build Your Avatar Document: Identify where your ideal clients typically look for vendors like you and what their budget range is for projects similar to yours.
Build Your Avatar Document: Treat your Client Avatar Document as a living reference point and pull it out every time you're considering a new client opportunity to quickly assess fit.
Know Your Pricing Message: Understand that your pricing sends a market signal about your availability, desperation level, and negotiating room that attracts matching clients.
Know Your Pricing Message: Recognize that a low price doesn't just mean affordable it signals you might be desperate, available, and willing to negotiate downward.
Know Your Pricing Message: Use this understanding to strategically raise your rates because higher prices filter out problem clients and attract those who respect your value.
Know Your Pricing Message: Track your Client Avatar and pricing together so that rate increases are aligned with your ideal client profile and attract the right segment.
